title: Duranta erecta
wikitext:
{{Short description|Species of flowering plant}} {{speciesbox |image = Duranta erecta serres du Luxembourg.jpg |image_caption = |status = LC |status_system = IUCN3.1 |status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Botanic Gardens Conservation International (BGCI) |author2=IUCN SSC Global Tree Specialist Group |year=2019 |title=''Duranta erecta'' |article-number=e.T145351548A145351550 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2019-2.RLTS.T145351548A145351550.en |access-date=25 November 2022}} |genus = Duranta |species = erecta |authority = [[Carl Linnaeus|L.]] |synonyms = ''Duranta repens'' L. }} '''''Duranta erecta''''' is a species of [[Flowering plant|flowering]] [[shrub]] in the [[verbena]] family [[Verbenaceae]], native from Mexico to South America and the [[Caribbean]]. It is widely cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] in [[Tropics|tropical]] and [[Subtropics|subtropical]] gardens throughout the world, and has become [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in many places. Common names include '''golden dewdrop''', '''pigeon berry''', and '''skyflower'''. ==Description== [[File:Golden Dewdrop (Duranta erecta).jpg|thumb|left|250px|Cascading flowers]] [[File:Pingo-de-ouro, ou violeteira (Duranta erecta) - 55224238263.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Fruits]] ''Duranta erecta'' is a sprawling [[shrub]] or (infrequently) a small [[tree]]. It can grow to {{convert|6|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall and can spread to an equal width. Mature specimens possess axillary [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|thorns]], which are often absent on younger specimens. The [[leaf|leaves]] are light green, elliptic to ovate, opposite, and grow up to {{convert|7.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} broad, with a 1.5 cm petiole. The [[flower]]s are light-blue or lavender, produced in tight [[Inflorescence|clusters]] located on terminal and axillary stems, sometimes appearing as [[panicles]], frequently recurved or pendulous, blooming in summer. The [[fruit]] is a small globose yellow or orange [[Berry (botany)|berry]], up to {{convert|11|mm|in|abbr=on}} diameter and containing several [[seed]]s.Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening'' 2: 117. Macmillan {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}. ==Taxonomy== The genus name is in honor of [[Castore Durante]], a fifteenth-century Italian botanist.{{cite web |url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287483 |title=Duranta erecta |publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]] |access-date=2008-12-11}} The [[specific name (botany)|specific epithet]] ''erecta'' means "upright" in [[Latin]]. The plant is also known as ''D. repens'', from the Latin for "creeping". The latter name was originally used to identify smaller-leaved [[Variety (botany)|varieties]] of the species.{{cite web |url=http://okeechobee.ifas.ufl.edu/News%20columns/Duranta.Golden.Dewdrop.htm |title= Add drops of Gold to Florida Yards |publisher=[[University of Florida]] [[Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences]] |author=Culbert, D. F. |access-date=2008-12-11}} ==Ecology== ''Duranta erecta'' is native to the Americas, from Mexico and the [[Caribbean]] south to Brazil and Argentina. There is some debate about whether the plant is also native to the southern United States, in [[Florida]], [[Louisiana]], [[Texas]], [[Arizona]] and [[California]], or is an [[introduced species]] there, at an altitude of 40–1100 meters above sea level.{{cite web |url=http://www.floridata.com/ref/D/dura_ere.cfm |title=Floridata: Duranta erecta |publisher=Floridata |author=Christman, Steve |date=October 26, 2003 |access-date=2008-12-11}} In its natural state, it commonly grows in rocky or [[sand]]y [[coast]]al areas with full sun, or moister, [[Ruderal species|disturbed sites]] inland. Prior to maturity, the plant will grow at a rate of up to half a meter per year. ==Cultivation== [[Image:Pingo-de-ouro, ou violeteira (Duranta erecta) - 55224487405.jpg|thumb|Tree with hanging fruits in [[Brazil]]]] Golden dewdrop is widely grown as an [[ornamental plant]] throughout [[Tropics|tropical]] and warm [[Subtropics|subtropical]] regions. Its showy [[flower]]s and [[fruit]] make it a desirable addition to gardens, and the blossoms attract [[Butterfly|butterflies]] and [[hummingbird]]s. There are a wide variety of [[cultivar]]s available, including 'Alba', 'Aurea', 'Aussie Gold', 'Gold Mound', 'Geisha Girl', 'Sapphire Showers', and 'Variegata'.{{cite web |url=http://okeechobee.ifas.ufl.edu/News%20columns/Duranta.Cultivars.htm |title=Duranta cultivars |publisher=[[University of Florida]] [[Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences]] |author=Culbert, D. F. |access-date=2008-12-11}} ===Invasive potential=== The plant has been identified as an [[invasive species]] in Australia, South Asia, China, South Africa, [[Hawaii]], [[Fiji]] and [[French Polynesia]].{{cite web |url=http://www.hear.org/gcw/species/duranta_repens/ |title=Global Compendium of Weeds: Duranta repens |publisher=[[Hawaiian Ecosystems at Risk project]] |access-date=2008-12-11}}{{cite web |url=http://www.hear.org/Pier/species/duranta_erecta.htm |title=Pacific Islands Ecosystems at Risk: Duranta erecta |publisher=[[Hawaiian Ecosystems at Risk project]] |access-date=2008-12-11}} It has been introduced to other habitats but has not become invasive. == Properties== The leaves and unripened berries of the plant are [[Toxin|toxic]], and are confirmed to have killed dogs and cats.{{cite web |url=http://awsassets.wwf.org.au/downloads/sp127_poisonous_and_invasive_plants_in_australia_1jul07.pdf |title=Poisonous Plants in Australia: Enabling consumers to buy safe plants |author=Thompson, N |year=2007 |publisher=[[World Wide Fund for Nature|WWF]]-Australia |page=10 |access-date=2008-12-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110103830/http://awsassets.wwf.org.au/downloads/sp127_poisonous_and_invasive_plants_in_australia_1jul07.pdf |archive-date=2014-01-10 }} However, [[songbird]]s eat the fruit without ill effects.{{cite web |url=http://www.fs.fed.us/global/iitf/pdf/shrubs/Duranta%20erecta.pdf |title=Duranta erecta |publisher=[[United States Forest Service]] |author=Francis, John K. |access-date=2008-12-11}} Documented cases of toxicity in humans are sparse, with many secondary sources stating that children have died from consumption of the plant. This is likely attributable to an 1895 case of presumed poisoning by ''Duranta erecta'' (formerly ''Duranta plumieri'') in a four year-old boy in Australia. From the original text:{{Cite journal |last=Wheeler |first=J. A. |date=20 Aug 1895 |title=A Fatal Case of Poisoning, Presumably by Berries of Duranta Plumieri |url=https://archive.org/details/australasianmed12unkngoog/page/338/mode/2up |journal=The Australasian Medical Gazette |volume=XIV |pages=338–339 |via=Boston Medical Library Association}}
"[A]bout 3:30 p.m. he said he felt very tired and sleepy. [...] His face was very flushed and the pupils dilated, while his lips and eyelids appeared swollen. [...] At 7 p.m. the boy had passed a large motion [sic] into the bed. This was sticky, ashy-grey in colour. [...] The tongue was coated with a dirty-grey fur, and the breath had the same offensive smell as the motions. The lips were slightly swollen and cracked, but not discoloured, and the tonsils and back of the pharynx were very red, but not swollen. [T]he conjunctivae were injected. [...] The pupils were dilated, very little iris being visible, and they were insensitive to light. [...] The temperature was 105.4 °F. [The] pulse was 200. About 5 a.m. he began to convulse, the spasms being tonic in character, with slight opisthotonos and marked retraction of the head. During the spasms the eyes were widely opened and the pupils less dilated, while the [facial muscles] did not participate in the general spasm, and the jaws were not tightly clenched. At 7 a.m. the temperature had fallen to 101 °F and the pulse to 160. [He vomited] inky-looking liquid material, the fluid part of which was colourless, and the solid portion like coffee grounds. The convulsive attacks now became more frequent and prolonged, [and] he died at 10:45 a.m. [A] small portion of [feces] passed about a quarter of an hour before death was scraped from the bed clothes and washed, when a number of partly digested berries of the ''Duranta plumieri'' was found in it. [...] I am not aware that the toxicology of ''Duranta'' has ever been investigated, but the symptoms described above, taken with the presence of berries in the motions, appear to bear the relation of effect and cause. If this is so, it would appear to be a poison of a cerebrospinal type [...]. It is of course dangerous to theorize too much on such a slender basis as a single case, and that but incompletely observed, but I think that the combination of circumstances described in the above report is a very strong piece of ''prima facie'' evidence for the conclusions arrived at."
[[Antioxidative]] [[coumarinolignoid]]s called [[repenin]]s have been isolated from ''Duranta erecta''.{{Cite journal|last1=Ahmad|first1=Nisar|last2=Zeb|first2=Fozia|last3=Ahmad|first3=Ijaz|last4=Wang|first4=Fanghai|date=2009-07-01|title=Repenins A-D, four new antioxidative coumarinolignoids from Duranta repens Linn|journal=Bioorganic & Medicinal Chemistry Letters|volume=19|issue=13|pages=3521–3524|doi=10.1016/j.bmcl.2009.05.006|issn=1464-3405|pmid=19464173}} In the fruit, the [[alkaloid]] [[isoquinoline]] in addition to the [[monoterpenes]] durantoside I, durantoside, and repenoside have been identified.{{cn|date=July 2023}} The leaves and fruits of ''D. repens'' contain a [[saponin]] glycoside and the presence of [[hydrocyanic acid]]. The durantoside has been detected in leaves and stems with leaves. The isoquinoline is lethal to insects.{{cn|date=July 2023}} ==Gallery== File:Duranta erecta (38) 1200.jpg|Duranta erecta File:Close Up - Flowers Golden Duranta Bush.jpg|Duranta Flowers File:Golden Duranta Bush with flowers.jpg|Duranta Bush File:Duranta erecta Sapphire Blue 1zz.jpg|'Saphhire Blue' cultivar File:Colius White-backed mousebird feeding on Duranta berries 9859.jpg|[[Mousebird]] feeding on fruit File:Duranta erecta 001.jpg|A large shrub File:Duranta erecta (1) 1200.jpg|Flower closeup File:Starr 070221-4825 Duranta erecta.jpg|Small hedge File:Starr-090421-6238-Duranta erecta-flowering and fruiting habit-Pukalani-Maui (24656859320).jpg|Grown as a small tree File:Duranta erecta sapphire showes-3-the regent hill-yercaud-salem-India.JPG|A sprawling shrub in India File:Duranta erecta plant showing its fruits.jpg|Fruits closeup ==References== {{Commons category}} {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20071016054047/http://www.sdhortsoc.org/duranta.htm|title=Durable, Dependable: Durantas!|sec=el}} (San Diego Horticultural Society, via the Internet Archive) * {{AfricanPlants|Duranta erecta}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q2732360}} [[Category:Verbenaceae]] [[Category:Flora of the Caribbean]] [[Category:Flora of Central America]] [[Category:Flora of Mexico]] [[Category:Flora of Southern America]] [[Category:Garden plants]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]] [[Category:Flora of Nepal]] [[Category:Flora without expected TNC conservation status]]
